_comment: Site-card explanations. {site} and {target} are replaced by the UI. Keep each sentence under 30 words.

T.why: Slope and surface roughness affect landing safety, rover routes and equipment access.
T.strong: Slopes and roughness at {site} fall within the range measured at {target}.
T.partial: The broad terrain resembles {target}, but local slopes or roughness differ.
T.breaks: Terrain at {site} differs from {target}; landing and mobility tests may not transfer.

H.why: Thermal response helps characterize surface materials, while temperature sets equipment limits.
H.strong: Surface heating and cooling at {site} resemble conditions measured at {target}.
H.partial: Thermal response is similar, but absolute temperatures differ.
H.breaks: Thermal conditions at {site} differ from {target}; temperature-sensitive tests may not transfer.

M.why: Rock type and brightness affect instrument readings, sample science and surface behavior.
M.strong: Rock type and surface brightness at {site} resemble {target}.
M.partial: Some rock types overlap, but the dominant materials differ.
M.breaks: The rocks at {site} differ from {target}; mineral and sample tests may not transfer.

W.why: Water and ice distribution guide resource prospecting and help interpret possible biosignatures.
W.strong: Water or ice conditions at {site} resemble those reported at {target}.
W.partial: Both sites have relevant water conditions, but abundance or form differs.
W.breaks: Water conditions at {site} differ from {target}; ice or resource tests may not transfer.

B.why: Local life can alter soil chemistry and complicate biosignature detection or contamination control.
B.strong: Sparse visible life at {site} supports some contamination-control tests for {target} missions.
B.partial: Some biological activity is present, so contamination controls need careful interpretation.
B.breaks: Biological activity at {site} differs from {target}; biosignature tests need contamination controls.

C.why: Slope, soil strength and excavability affect foundations, grading, landing pads and construction access.
C.strong: Measured slope and ground properties at {site} resemble those at {target} for construction trials.
C.partial: Some construction conditions match, but slope or ground properties differ from {target}.
C.breaks: This ground could not stand in for {target}: Earth tests prove the surface, not the construction environment on the Moon or Mars.

A.why: Wind and airborne dust affect visibility, solar power and equipment wear.
A.strong: Wind and dust conditions at {site} resemble those measured at {target}.
A.partial: Dust is present, but wind or particle transport differs from {target}.
A.breaks: The atmosphere at {site} differs from {target}; dust transport tests may not transfer.

I.why: Low sun angles create long shadows and high contrast that challenge polar navigation and operations.
I.strong: Sun angles at {site} reproduce the low-angle lighting measured at {target}.
I.partial: Low-angle light occurs at {site}, but not as consistently as at {target}.
I.breaks: Sun angles at {site} differ from {target}; lighting and shadow tests may not transfer.

moon: Lunar gravity is one-sixth of Earth's; dust motion, slope stability and crew movement differ.
Hard vacuum, so heat moves only by radiation and conduction, never by air.
The Moon lacks a global magnetic field and atmosphere, leaving its surface exposed to radiation.
Permanently shadowed lunar regions can reach roughly 25–40 K, colder than natural Earth environments.
A lunar day lasts about 29.5 Earth days, including roughly two weeks of darkness.
Lunar regolith is sharp and unweathered; Earth's soils have often been altered by water and wind.
mars: Martian gravity is about three-eighths of Earth's.
Mars has a thin carbon-dioxide atmosphere, about 6 mbar, that cannot carry heat like Earth's air.
Mars lacks a global magnetic field, so surface radiation exceeds typical Earth conditions.
Martian soil contains perchlorate salts that most Earth analog soils do not.
Martian surface temperatures vary widely, roughly from 140 to 300 K.
earth_side: Earth biology is everywhere, so any site is a contamination source for biosignature tests.
construction_note: Earth tests can measure whether a site is flat enough for pads, roads, grading and equipment access.
They can test trenching, compaction, foundations and robotic construction workflows in real soil.
They can test dust control, material handling and building prototypes with local materials.
They cannot reproduce lunar or Martian gravity, which changes footing loads, slope stability and dust behavior.
They cannot reproduce vacuum, radiation or extreme thermal cycling, which affect seals, joints and materials.
They cannot prove long-term survival in sharp, dry regolith, where excavation and wear differ from Earth soil.
